HomePage.headline: Turning ideas into reality and building experiences through <highlight>logic and imagination!</highlight>
HomePage.intro: Hi! I'm , an early-career Full-Stack developer with a technical degree from SENAC and a Game Developer in training at Unisinos. I work mainly with TypeScript, Next.js, and Express for web development, as well as Unity for game creation. My goal is to turn your ideas into code!
HomePage.imageAlt: Stylized illustration representing the portfolio author.
HomePage.aboutMeFirstParagraph: I'm Bruno Nunes, an early-career full-stack developer and a game developer in training. I'm passionate about turning simple ideas into digital experiences, from web applications to playable worlds.
HomePage.aboutMeSecondParagraph: Currently, my main focus is on TypeScript, Next.js, Express, and Unity, technologies that allow me to create real and impactful projects. This focus began during my technical education at SENAC, where I learned essential frontend, backend, and database concepts, in addition to deepening my knowledge independently.

info.name: Minerva
info.description: An application for teaching logic and programming in a gamified way, featuring a lesson system, user progress tracking, and interactive challenges.
text: This application aims to help young people learn logic and programming through gamification. It offers clear explanations and practical challenges covering the fundamental concepts of programming.
The platform includes user authentication, password encryption, a clean architecture with dependency inversion, automated tests, and the ability to be used without requiring registration.
The frontend was developed in TypeScript to reduce development-time errors; Next.js, leveraging components, routing, and caching; and Tailwind CSS to simplify the creation of responsive interfaces.
The backend also uses TypeScript, with Express to simplify communication between frontend and backend, and Prisma ORM for more efficient and secure database management.

info.name: Loja-Loja
info.description: Online store with a product catalog and authentication stored in the database, and a shopping cart saved on the user's computer.
text: This is an online store with fictional products that offers an authentication system, PDF generation at checkout, and a shopping cart persisted locally on the user's device.
The frontend was developed using HTML for application structure, CSS for visual styling, and JavaScript to implement interactions and dynamic behavior.
The backend was implemented in JavaScript using Express for communication between client and server, along with a relational MySQL database managed using the mysql2 library.

info.name: Pokemon
info.description: A game in which the user must guess which Pokémon it is based on its silhouette.
text: This application is a game inspired by the classic "Who's That Pokémon?", where only the silhouette of a Pokémon is shown and the player must try to guess which one it is.

The frontend was developed using pure HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The public PokeAPI was used to provide Pokémon names and images, which were transformed into silhouettes using the CSS brightness property.

info.course: Technical High School in Web Development
info.additionalInfo: Technical education integrated with High School
description: A course focused on web application development and building a solid foundation in programming and technology.
Covers website and web application development using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, including responsive design concepts, best structuring practices, and accessibility.
Includes programming logic, backend development with Node.js and Express, modeling and usage of relational databases (MySQL), as well as code versioning with Git and GitHub.

info.additionalInfo: Undergraduate technologist degree in the digital games field
description: A program focused on digital game development, covering both technical and creative aspects of the field.
Includes fundamentals of game programming, 2D and 3D game development, use of game engines, as well as mathematics, physics, and artificial intelligence concepts applied to games.
Also covers game design, narrative, user experience, asset production, multidisciplinary teamwork, and practices of the digital games industry.

hero.title: Who I Am
hero.description: Hi! I'm <Bruno Nunes>, an early-career Full-Stack developer with a technical background from SENAC and a Game Developer in training at Unisinos. I work mainly with TypeScript, Next.js, and Express for web development, as well as Unity for game creation. My goal is to turn your ideas into code!

journey.title: My Journey into Programming
journey.paragraph1: I had my first contact with programming at the age of 11, when I watched the video "<link>The Games I Made When I Was a Kid</link>". At the time, I tried to learn several times but always ended up quitting. My programming journey truly began around the age of 15, when I entered a technical school and started coding more consistently. It was love at second sight. I've always been fascinated by understanding how things work "behind the screen".
journey.paragraph2: After many attempts, broken code, and endless Google searches, I realized that creating software was something that deeply motivated me. Over time, this curiosity turned into a professional goal. I began studying HTML, CSS, and JavaScript outside of school as well, creating small interactions and trying to replicate features I saw on other websites.
journey.paragraph3: At the same time, I started pursuing another major interest: game development. Initially as a hobby, I began creating small games and prototypes in Unity, using programming as a way to combine logic and creativity. Today, I continue studying daily to expand my technical skill set and develop increasingly complete and well-structured projects.

motivation.title: What Motivates Me
motivation.paragraph1: What excites me most about programming is the feeling of turning an idea into something tangible. Whether it's an application, an interface, a system, or a game, seeing something work because of lines I wrote is an incredible feeling.
motivation.paragraph2: I'm also driven by challenges: I enjoy understanding complex problems and breaking them down into smaller parts until I find a solution. Finally, I believe in the power of technology to create meaningful, innovative, useful, or simply fun experiences.

goals.title: What I'm Looking For
goals.paragraph1: I'm looking for opportunities where I can grow as a developer and take part in projects that combine creativity, technical skills, and good practices. I enjoy environments where code is well thought out, organized, and evolves over time.
goals.paragraph2: I value working with people who enjoy building things and sharing knowledge. To me, learning and teaching are part of a fundamental process.
goals.paragraph3: My goal is to create solutions that make a difference, whether in efficient applications or engaging games, and to keep evolving constantly, one commit at a time.
